source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 13–15. The full original XML record at 14:48 includes a vowel annotation; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps being brought to the priest without implying entry into the camp; the following verse specifies the outside location.
Retains the priest's movement and healing before cleansing, rather than depicting the rite as a treatment that heals the disease.
Preserves two living clean birds and all three materials; takes the procurement as the priest's command without inventing a named assistant.
Retains commanded slaughter, fresh living water and clay vessel; does not make the bird an altar sin offering.
Keeps the staged restoration: clean and within the camp but still outside the person's own tent for seven days.
Preserves sex and number of lambs, explicit age only for the female, and both ancient quantities. Ephah supplies the understood dry-measure unit.
Retains the explicit ish here as man and presents both person and offerings; does not silently remove the sex-specific formulation.
Keeps the specified holy slaughter location, priestly entitlement and most-holy classification without identifying this place with the inner sanctuary.
Keeps sin offering as the established term but specifies impurity as the stated context; does not invent a personal offense or a forgiveness formula. Passive slaughter leaves the unstated agent open.
Preserves poverty and the hand-reaching affordability idiom, reduced flour, unchanged guilt lamb and unchanged oil quantity.
Names the priest as the continued actor; the source's singular one is expressed in the resumed one/other construction in verse 31, keeping the offering sentence readable across labels.
Preserves the repeated affordability clause and expresses the resumed one/other pair across the verse boundary; no third bird is implied.
Keeps the concluding affordability condition and supplies offerings as the contextual object of the hand-reaching idiom.
Retains Canaan, possession and the LORD's explicit agency in placing the affliction; does not convert it into a merely natural event or a punishment explanation.
Keeps the owner's report tentative through ke-nega; the owner does not pronounce the house unclean.
Preserves emptying before inspection and the stated protection of contents from impurity, without rewriting it as a disinfection procedure.
Preserves renewed examination, spreading, mammeret classification and the house's status without diagnosing a particular fungus.
Keeps the complete demolition and all three materials, rendering priestly responsibility without suggesting he alone performs the work.
Preserves the source's healing language for the house as well as its clean verdict; full XML hash retains the source's vowel annotation.
Retains the outside-city release and atonement for a house, preventing the assumption that every atonement formula names personal moral guilt.
Maintains the human/material link through defiling and the explanatory vocabulary; retains both object classes.
Preserves the teaching purpose and final category summary, using both contextual English terms to represent the Hebrew's single broader tsaraat category.
